_comment: Declared output fields that are ABSENT from a real response under the operation's own
default inputs, each with a verdict and the evidence for it. Read by scripts/contract-check.mjs.
TWO VERDICTS, and the distinction is the whole point of this file:
conditional — the field is REAL and the declaration is CORRECT. It simply does not appear
for the input the check happens to send (a different mode, an optional input
absent). Verified present under the stated input. Reported, never failed:
failing here would be the guard lying about a working contract.
phantom     — the field is NOT returned under ANY input found. This is the real defect,
the same class as the five fields `Calculate Consignment` advertised and
/api/consignment had never returned. Reported with its correct name where one
exists, and NOT failed only because it PREDATES this guard — see the baseline
note below.
THE BASELINE, stated plainly so it cannot be mistaken for coverage: this guard landed on
2026-08-08 and found 13 of 20 operations already declaring at least one absent field. Failing
on all of them on day one would have meant landing a permanently-red check, which is how a
guard gets disabled. So the pre-existing set is recorded here and the guard is PROSPECTIVE:
any absence NOT listed below fails the run. Every entry below is a live customer-facing
defect — a user who maps one of these gets an empty value on every run — and the phantom
list IS the pre-publish worklist for the Zapier public listing.
Rules, same discipline as the vehicle-truth waivers in the freighttools repo:
- `field` must match an absent key EXACTLY. An entry matching nothing is a FAILURE, not a
no-op: stale paperwork reads as coverage exactly like an unwired guard does.
- `why` must carry evidence — the real field name, or the input under which it appears.
- Fixing one means deleting its entry in the same change. The guard then holds the line.
